input.question: if atoms and particles have "rest mass" or "rest mass energy" when they're moving is their mass different? how does the higgs field relate to rest mass?
input.ground_truth: People used to define masses which change based on how the object is moving, but they are ugly and generally an unnecessary concept. These days "mass" and "rest mass" mean the exact same thing. Rest energy is just rest mass times c^(2). The Higgs mechanism gives certain particles some of their (rest) masses in the standard model of particle physics.

Now, if you push the toy car and it starts rolling really fast, it’s a little harder to stop or pick up. In the same way, when a tiny particle moves really fast, it acts like it’s a little heavier. But when it stops, it goes back to its “rest mass.”

Now, about the Higgs field: Imagine the Higgs field is like a big, soft blanket that covers everything. When a tiny particle moves through this blanket, the blanket sticks to it a little. So, rest mass is how heavy something feels when it’s not moving, and the Higgs field helps give things that weight! 🧸🚗✨
